The [[RA-7 protocol droid]] '''4D6-J-A7''' served the [[Galactic Empire]]'s [[Imperial Intelligence]] and [[Imperial Security Bureau]] as an administrative [[Aide|assistant]] during the [[Imperial Era|Age of the Empire]]. As a result of intrusion protection applied on her databanks, 4D6-J-A7 developed a conceited attitude that led to her looking down on other [[droid]]s of lower station. She was present in the Empire's [[Citadel Tower]] on the [[planet]] [[Scarif]] when a [[Battle of Scarif|battle]] against the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance]] began, which culminated in the tower's destruction by the Empire's [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]] [[superweapon]].

==Biography==
4D6-J-A7 was an [[RA-7 protocol droid]] who served as an administrative [[Aide|assistant]] in [[Imperial Intelligence]] and in the [[Imperial Security Bureau]].<ref name="ROUVG" /> During the [[Imperial Era|reign]] of the Empire, she was stationed in the [[Imperial Office of Security]] in the [[Citadel Tower]],<ref name="Geektionary">''[[Star Wars: Geektionary: The Galaxy from A - Z]]''</ref> a structure containing the archival [[Scarif vault]], located in the [[Imperial Center of Military Research|Imperial security complex]] on the [[planet]] [[Scarif]].<ref name="ROUVG" />

[[File:4D6-J-A7_and_officers.png|thumb|left|180px|4D6-J-A7 was stationed in the Citadel Tower.]]
In the [[Standard year|year]] [[1 BBY]],<ref name="Date">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'', including 4D6-J-A7's appearance on [[Scarif]], to [[1 BBY]].</ref> she was present in the tower when [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance]] [[agent]]s [[Jyn Erso]],<ref name="RO" /> [[Cassian Jeron Andor]]<ref name="ROUVG" /> and [[K-2SO]] infiltrated the structure disguised as Imperial staff. The Alliance trio passed 4D6-J-A7 within the tower while the [[Protocol droid|droid]] was conversing with a pair of [[Imperial officer]]s,<ref name="RO" /> but she failed to recognize the infiltrators as a real threat to the Empire.<ref name="Geektionary" /> The [[Battle of Scarif]] broke out soon after, resulting in the Alliance's theft of the [[Death Star plans|plans]] to the Empire's [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]] [[superweapon]] and the destruction of the Citadel Tower by the Death Star itself.<ref name="RO" />

==Characteristics==
[[File:4D6-J-A7-ROUSE.png|right|thumb|200px|4D6-J-A7 was regularly exposed to classified information.]]
Manufactured by [[Arakyd Industries]],<ref name="CEUE" /> 4D6-J-A7 had [[Gender|feminine]] programming;<ref name="Geektionary" /> [[Color|black]] [[sensor]]s<ref name="RO" /> and distinctive, glossy black plating;<ref name="Geektionary" /> and, like all RA-7 protocol [[droid]]s, stood 1.7 [[meter]]s (5 [[Foot|feet]], 7 inches) tall.<ref name="AEYNTKUE" /> Given that 4D6-J-A7 was regularly exposed to highly classified information, her [[databank]]s were protected from electronic or other forms of intrusion. This,<ref name="ROUVG" /> and her high rank,<ref name="Geektionary" /> led to her developing a conceited attitude<ref name="ROUVG" /> and acting in a mean<ref name="Geektionary" /> and insufferably arrogant manner to droids of a lower station, neither of which affected her performance on Scarif.<ref name="ROUVG" />

==Behind the scenes==
4D6-J-A7 was portrayed by [[Nathan Plant]]<ref name="Dee Tails interview">{{WebCite|url=https://www.starwarsinterviews.com/star-wars-anthology/rogue-one/dee-tails-k-ohn|text=Dee Tails (K-OHN)|author=Pellegrom, Dennis|work=[https://www.starwarsinterviews.com Star Wars Interviews]|archivedate=20171209201513|nolive=1}}</ref> in the [[2016]] [[Star Wars Anthology Series|''Anthology'']] film, ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]''.<ref name="RO" /> Plant also portrayed another RA-7 droid in ''Rogue One'',<ref name="Dee Tails interview" /> [[KMD-RA-71]],<ref name="ROUVG" /> as well as one of the [[Hassk triplets]] [[Star Wars: Episode VII The Force Awakens|''Star Wars'': Episode VII ''The Force Awakens'']],<ref name="Dee Tails interview" /> the [[2015]] [[sequel trilogy]] film.<ref name="TFA">{{Film|VII}}</ref> 4D6-J-A7 was not identified in the film<ref name="RO" /> but was given a designation by [[Pablo Hidalgo]] in the reference book ''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]'',<ref name="ROUVG" /> which was released on the same day as the film.<ref name="Book Date">{{SW|url=news/rebel-reading-rogue-one-books|text=Rebel Reading: A Guide to ''Rogue One'' Books}}</ref>
